author: Sunflower State News
title: William Allen White Book Award celebration to be held at Emporia State University
text:
Students and educators from across Kansas will gather on Oct. 3 for the 74th annual William Allen White Children’s Book Awards at Emporia State University, according to an April 29 announcement. The event is free and open to the public.
The awards recognize outstanding children’s literature as chosen by Kansas schoolchildren. Authors Shannon Earle and Angela Cervantes will attend as guests of honor, with Earle receiving recognition for “The Penguin of Ilha Grande: From Animal Rescue to Extraordinary Friendship,” selected by students in Grades 3 through 5, and Cervantes being honored for “The Cursed Moon,” chosen by voters in Grades 6 through 8.
All activities will take place in the William Allen White Library, with the awards ceremony scheduled for Albert Taylor Hall inside Plumb Hall. Attendees can check in starting at 8:30 a.m., meet the authors, have books autographed, participate in arts and crafts projects, and purchase copies of both winning books. The ceremony begins at 11 a.m., with no food or drink allowed inside the auditorium.
The William Allen White Children’s Book Award is described as the oldest statewide children’s book award in the United States. It was established in 1952 by Ruth Garver Gagliardo, a children’s literature specialist at Emporia State University, to honor William Allen White—an American author, politician, leader of the Progressive movement, and editor of The Emporia Gazette.
Supported by organizations including the Trusler Foundation and Emporia State University Libraries & Archives, The White Awards Program aims to encourage Kansas children to read quality books. More information about this year’s events can be found at wawchildrensbookaward.com.
